cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend, because this one's a letter. Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, is writing to Timothy. Paul already sent him one letter, so this is round two.

cards.question: Before Paul gets to anything else, he tells Timothy what Timothy is to him. What does Paul call him?

cards.text: Beloved child gets me RIGHT in the handle, friend, because I've got six little ones who call me Papa. Then Paul thanks God, whom he serves with a clear conscience, as his forefathers did.

cards.question: Paul thanks God as he remembers Timothy in his prayers. True or false: Paul says he remembers Timothy night and day.

cards.text: Then Paul brings up Timothy's tears. The letter doesn't say why Timothy cried, but I bet Paul can still see that moment like it was yesterday.

cards.question: Remembering Timothy's tears, what does Paul long for?

answers.text: To see Timothy and be filled with joy
To bring Timothy along on his travels
To know Timothy is safe and resting

cards.text: Next Paul is reminded of Timothy's sincere faith. And Paul says Timothy isn't the first one in his family to have it.

cards.question: Where did Timothy's sincere faith first dwell?

answers.text: In his grandmother and his mother
In his father and his grandfather
In his uncle and his older brother

cards.text: Grandma Lois, then mom Eunice, and Paul is convinced it's in Timothy too. Some families hand down a cookie recipe, but THIS family handed down faith three generations deep.
For this reason, Paul reminds Timothy about the gift of God that's in him. It came through the laying on of Paul's hands.

cards.question: What does Paul tell Timothy to do with the gift of God that's in him?

cards.text: Friend, I run ovens all day, and a fire nobody tends goes OUT. Then Paul tells Timothy what kind of spirit God has given us.

cards.question: Paul writes, God has not given us a spirit of ___, but of power, love, and self-control.

cards.text: Power, love, and self-control. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer jumping every time somebody pulled it open, so I needed that verse back then, baby.

cards.question: God's spirit isn't one of fear. So what does Paul tell Timothy not to be ashamed of?
Paul also tells Timothy not to be ashamed of Paul himself. What does Paul call himself in that line?
Instead of being ashamed, Paul asks Timothy to join him in suffering for the gospel. True or false: Paul says to do it by Timothy's own strength.

cards.text: Then Paul steps back to the big picture. God has saved us and called us to a holy calling.

cards.question: According to Paul, what's behind God saving us and calling us to a holy calling?

answers.text: The good works we have done

cards.question: True or false: Paul says God granted this grace in Christ Jesus before time began.

cards.text: God had grace ready before time began, and I can't plan a batch two days out. Now, Paul says, that grace has been revealed through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus.

cards.question: Christ Jesus has abolished ___ and illuminated the way to life and immortality through the gospel.

cards.text: After years in a dark junk drawer, the word illuminated makes me want to stand up and HOLLER. And this is the gospel Paul was appointed to as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher.
Paul doesn't pretend it's easy. He's suffering, and he says so.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says his suffering has made him ashamed.
Paul is suffering, but he isn't ashamed. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He knows whom he has believed
He knows his suffering will end soon
He knows the church stands with him

cards.text: And Paul is convinced He is able to guard what Paul has entrusted to Him for that day. Friend, I once lost a whole bag of chocolate chips INSIDE my own apron, so I respect a Guard like that.

Then Paul turns it back to Timothy: hold on to the pattern of sound teaching he heard from Paul, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus. And guard the treasure entrusted to him, so there's that word entrusted again.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to guard the treasure entrusted to him. Who does Paul say helps him do it?

answers.text: The Holy Spirit who dwells in us
The elders who prayed over him
The believers who serve beside him

cards.text: Now Paul gets honest about how things are going. Everyone in the province of Asia has deserted him, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
EVERYONE, friend, like posting in the group chat and watching every single person leave it. Then Paul writes, "May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus," and he's got a reason.

cards.question: Why does Paul want the Lord to grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus?

answers.text: He often refreshed Paul and wasn't ashamed of his chains
He paid a large sum to get Paul released from prison
He took over teaching the churches Paul had started

cards.question: When Onesiphorus arrived in Rome, he ___ diligently until he found Paul.

cards.text: Friend, I know what it means when somebody comes looking for you in the dark. Paul writes, "May the Lord grant Onesiphorus His mercy on that day."

cards.question: True or false: Paul says Timothy knows very well how much Onesiphorus ministered to him in Ephesus.

findings.problem: The card says Paul already sent Timothy one letter. That fact comes from outside the passage, and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Timothy appears here for the first time, but the card never says who he is (for example, Paul's coworker, with a reference such as Acts 16:1-3). The card only says Paul is writing to him.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card repeats "Power, love, and self-control" from verse 7, which the baker just answered, and adds a junk drawer joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so it works as a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The right answer, "The testimony of our Lord," sounds like Bible wording. The wrong answers, "His lack of experience" and "His humble background," sound modern and personal. The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 6 of the 9 choice cards in stop 1. True or false appears 2 times and fill in the blank 1 time, so multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card states "God had grace ready before time began," which is the content of 2 Timothy 1:9. The card cites only 2 Timothy 1:10, so the citation is narrower than the verses the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Onesiphorus appears here for the first time without being introduced, and so do Phygelus and Hermogenes on card 13. The only thing the text says about Onesiphorus is what he did for Paul. Cards 15 and 16 ask about exactly that, so introducing him would give those answers away. Phygelus and Hermogenes are not described anywhere in the passage.
findings.question: When the only thing known about a new person is the detail a later choice card asks about, or when the text gives no description at all, should the new-people rule give way to the never-give-away rule? Is something like "a man named Onesiphorus" enough?
